newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: Lion result gets mixed reviews, shares up.
newsitem.headline: Lion result gets mixed reviews, shares up.

text.p: Australasian brewer Lion Nathan Ltd's annual profit result got mixed reviews on Thursday but its share price rose seven cents to $3.64 in late morning trade.
The $150.4 million net profit, down from $202.3 million, was at the upper end of expectations. Earnings from operations rose 8.1 percent to NZ$246.6 million.

"The operating performance of the group was slightly ahead of market consensus, with Australia obviously being the main area of difficulty," said Doyle Paterson Brown analyst David Stanley. "The group profit before abnormals was about seven
However, John Cairns, head of research at Cavill White Securities, was less impressed.
"I thought it was a fairly ordinary result. The key to it is the performance in Australia, where, even adjusting for the exchange rate, their earnings are actually in a state of decline.
"I would have thought that was something the market hadn't been anticipating. Their touted cost savings in Australia really haven't kicked in to offset the slippage in market share," he said.
Cairns said he was surprised at the share price movement.
"I wouldn't think there was anything for the market to get overly positive about," he said.
Lion confirmed its market share in Australia dropped to 42.0 percent from 43.4 percent and operating earnings there fell 2.8 percent.
Stanley said fears about performance in Australia were alleviated by Lion's comments that it was only in the light beer market that it had lost market share.
"The market took some comfort from that," he said.
However, Cairns said he took no comfort from the fact that market share slippage was concentrated in one line.

"That amount of slippage is reasonably significant in a duopoly situation. Superficially, there is something more deep rooted than one product category. You have seen the upheaval on the management side of things over there. I don't think things are going as they would like," he said.
Tax provision was as anticipated even though Lion had to provide for $74.2 million tax against a credit of $1.8 million last year.
Cairns said Lion's New Zealand operations were seen as performing strongly and the strengthening of the balance sheet would be viewed positively.
Stanley suggested there could be more upside for the stock.

"The share price has been pretty weak for a couple of months now because people were concerned about things and what's happened is this result has come, provided a more solid basis for people to work from, and perhaps alleviated some fears."
